newsitem.title: UK: INSTANT VIEW - UK Nov, Dec trade data.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - UK Nov, Dec trade data.

text.p: Following is a selection of economists' reactions to UK trade data which showed a November world trade in goods deficit of 959 million stg (vs expected 761 million) and a non-EU trade deficit for December of 844 million stg (vs expected 663 million).

"It's quite disappointing on the global and non-EU front, mostly due to a drop in exports. Some people may say it's evidence of sterling strength but it's a bit too early for that. We see it more as an erratic number.

"One thing to look out for in next few months is the J-curve effect, where sterling strength will lead to a fall in import prices before any change in exports is possible, so the trade deficit will actually fall perversely in the early months, then start to widen. The general trend in 1997 will be to a worse trade deficit but I don't think this marks the start of that yet."

"The trade figures show a picture of disappointment on the non-EU side and the global picture for both months. There have been upward revisions to the shortfalls in previous months as well. Export volumes are well down in December for non-EU trade. That may well be a reflection of sterling's strength and will no doubt have an impact on domestic activity over the coming year. The sharp decline in import prices also reflects the performance of the currency during the period and should be favourable for the domestic inflation outlook over the next few months."

"The UK trade deficits are at the upper end of expectations and may be seen as a slight negative for the pound. Both global exports in November and non-EU exports in December fell and this will be seen by some as evidence of lost competitiveness, courtesy of sterling's climb...Given the relative strength of the UK economy vs key trading partners, some deterioration in the external accounts is only to be expected...At this stage would not see the red ink as a major worry and the pound should not be unduly concerned.

"Nonetheless, the trend is worsening and if core Europe in particular fails to recover, some nasty numbers may be in store down the road. This will help to slow growth, but the traditional threat from the balance of payments to UK growth prospects does not seem a big risk just yet."
